quality.review_scope: All six supplied main pages completely read and visually inspected; independent source, canonical, reader and private visual audits passed. No matched supporting information was located or verified; SI existence remains unverified and no absence is inferred. Preserve the unspecified basis of the approximately 500:1 water/Sn ratio, acid-set treatment pH versus unreported final TBAOH measurement pH, and radius/diameter/model distinctions. XRD is mentioned but the inspected article supplies no trace, SAED or atomic coordinates.
missing_fields: Main-only review; matched SI not located/verified and existence remains unverified. No SI supplied or inferred absent.
Refs7/25 contain fuller upstream synthesis; their full procedures have not been inspected in this extraction. No external downloads performed.
Absolute precursor and ethanol/water charges, water-ratio basis/order/rate, mixing, vessel, atmosphere, hydrolysis duration and oxidation conditions absent.
Dialysis membrane, water volume/exchange schedule, duration and chloride-removal endpoint absent.
Acid concentration/dose, TBAOH addition volume, post-redispersion pH, sonication power and final colloid concentration absent.
No numerical full spectral curves, tabulated peak/radius values, histogram particle list, or uncertainties for optical-derived radii. Original plots retained without invented digitization.

Cassiterite assignment is source-reported XRD prose; no XRD trace or SAED pattern supplied. No unit-cell constants, measured atom coordinates, CIF, surface ligands or full-particle atom model supplied.
No powder-isolation protocol, quantitative yield, PL quantum yield/lifetime, Raman data or sensor/device test supplied.
Mechanistic conclusions involve author assumptions, models and cited studies; sample atomistic dynamics and solution oxidation/speciation were not directly measured.
conflicts: Discussion identifies Figure4 HRTEM but parenthetical references say Figure3a/b; actual Figure3 is schematic. Figure4 captions and panels establish the imaging assignment.
Figure5 ordinate-independent horizontal variable is particle radius; Figure6b axis says Size but caption says radius from PL. Preserve radius and original labels, never silently use diameter.
The paper describes acid-set pH, then adds basic TBAOH after24h for spectra without reporting final pH. Treat plotted labels as treatment labels, not verified final measurement pH.
p3 proposes polycondensation rather than direct ion deposition, while conclusion p6 uses ion-deposition phrasing; these are retained author interpretations, not a resolved measured mechanism.

quality.review_scope: Independent scoped scientific quick audit accepted original main PDF pp.1–6 and matched SI pp.1–5, 8, 11–12: SI-made CdSe seeds and CdSe/CdS core/shell inputs, ensemble Ag+ titration including optical intermediates and 0%/107% XRD, single-dot 10 µM/75 µL/min Ag flow, four 5/10/20/40 µM Figure 3 conditions, and pure-methanol control. Only ensemble endpoint XRD has phase labels; intermediate optical responses are not structural phase measurements. SI-only rod and model branches and unrelated ancillary measurements remain outside this main-text unit. ACS source-figure publisher reuse permission remains unverified.
missing_fields: Initial CdSe/CdS concentration and solution volume for the ensemble titration are not reported; exact total Ag+ stoichiometry cannot be reconstructed.
No direct phase, composition map or atom-resolved structure is measured for the individual OFF-switching nanocrystals.
Per-concentration flow rates for Figure 3's 5/10/20/40 µM distributions are not restated; do not inherit Figure 2's 75 µL/min.
Exact temperature of AgNO3 exchange, shell thickness and final product size distribution are not reported in the scoped text.
No quantitative fraction of short-lived partially exchanged intermediate particles is measured by the single-dot PL readout.
Figure 1 intermediate 21/35/48/60/80% optical titration states have no separately reported XRD phases or individual-particle composition maps.
conflicts: Main Figure 2 visual last snapshot labels 12.4 s while the caption says 12.1 s; both are kept in figure provenance.
Main p.2 calls CdSe cores typically 3.5 nm; SI p.2 estimates 3.4 nm for synthesized CdSe seeds from an excitonic transition. These are distinct descriptions, not an averaged size.

Main Fig. 1 final diffraction is Ag2Se/Ag2S, while main prose sometimes shortens single-dot OFF outcome to Ag2Se; preserve two-component product identity and separate direct ensemble XRD from optical single-dot inference.

SI Figure S8 calls the control pure methanol with no AgNO3, but its last caption sentence reports AgNO3 concentration/flow settings. Do not assign AgNO3 to the negative-control reagent without resolving the contradiction.
Main Figure 4 is a stochastic simulation, not observed atomistic structures or additional synthesized specimens.

structure_assets.description: Figure 1: study-level pre-reduction CQD TEM/HRTEM, size, EDS and SAED; upstream CQD recipe is external. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 2: post-reduction Ag/CQD TEM/HRTEM, size, SAED, EDS/maps; visible d/e panel labels conflict with caption. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 3: XRD compares CQDs and Ag/CQDs; ~32.57° plane-label conflict (112 body versus 122 plot/caption). Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 3 CQD trace is an input comparator, not the Ag/CQD product trace. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 4 XPS supports Ag/carbon surface chemistry, not an atomic-coordinate model. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 5 FTIR input/product comparison supports surface-group interpretation only. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 6a baseline Ag/CQD SPR; other panels represent controls/series and are not its size/phase outcome. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 6b with-NH4OH spectrum lacks SPR; no corresponding branch TEM/XRD is supplied. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 6c has four volume labels without a reagent name; body/caption conflict, no structure series. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 7 input CQD zeta potential −4.91 mV; source figure comparison, not particle coordinates. Publisher permission unverified.
Figure 7 Ag/CQD product zeta potential −9.91 mV; source figure comparison, not particle coordinates. Publisher permission unverified.
SI Figure S1 is the authors' process schematic; heating/filter details conflict with main p.3. It is not measured structure. Publisher permission unverified.
Existing independent bulk fcc Ag reference; does not encode this Ag/CQD particle's coordinates, carbon support, surface or size.
Original symbolic CQD-stock identity card for the previously synthesized input; no atomistic model or measured particle geometry.
Original symbolic aqueous Ag/CQD route illustration; disputed main/SI heating stages are shown as unresolved, not selected conditions.

quality.review_scope: Independent scoped quick audit accepted main PDF pp.1–10 for the packaged Ag/CQD route, named optical comparison branches, Figures 1–7 and main-referred SI p.1 Figure S1. Main pp.11–13, the antibacterial assay/mechanism, SI pp.2–5 and upstream coal-to-CQD methods remain outside this synthesis–structure scope; this is not a complete-paper Reader.
missing_fields: Coal-to-CQD precursor preparation is delegated to references 37–39; this source supplies only the CQD stock concentration and 200 µL aliquot.
NH4OH branch lacks base volume/concentration linkage, addition order, stage temperatures/times and any measured size or phase.
Figure 6c four volume labels cannot be assigned to CQD or AgNO3 feed because body, caption and plot disagree/omit identity.
No sample-level batch/replicate map connects Figure 1 input CQDs or Figures 2–7 measurements to a unique physical aliquot.
Product ultrafiltration duration, wash volumes and retained fraction are not independently reported; main does not name a product-filter cutoff, while SI S1 labels 0.22 µm.
conflicts: Main PDF p.3 explicitly says 15-min mixing at room temperature and p.7 says 45-min reduction at room temperature; main-referred SI PDF p.1 Figure S1 marks heating (Δ) during both steps. Both reports are retained without selecting a reactor setpoint.

Figure 2 has three incompatible panel attributions: visible labels show (d) size and (e) SAED; p.4 body and caption call the size histogram (e), with caption assigning SAED to (d); p.5 body calls SAED (e). The visible panels support d=size/e=SAED, without treating the body as uniform.
Main PDF p.5 body assigns the ~32.57° XRD peak to (112), while Figure 3 plot/caption labels (122).

Main PDF p.7 body attributes Figure 6c to changing CQD concentration and a steady intensity decrease; Figure 6 caption calls it varying AgNO3 amount, the legend has only 50/100/200/400 µL, and plotted intensity is nonmonotonic. No dose–response or reagent assignment is inferred.

SI prints (0.2×0.5)/10=0.008 N; arithmetic gives 0.01 N. Conductometry uses 12 mL and reports 0.00833 N separately. Handling: Do not replace the reported value; retain displayed calculation and distinguish assays.
Main assigns low binding-energy O1s ~531.2 eV to C=O and high ~532.4 to C-OH; Table S2 reverses these group assignments. Handling: Keep each interpretation with its source locator.

SI prose carbonyl 162.35 ppm is absent from Figure S6 labelled peaks 161.298/159.630/...; main text uses isotope 19C while figure caption uses 13C; native/tagged CQD identity also ambiguous. Handling: 13C technique from caption, source typo retained. Do not assert unique molecular structure or native/tagged aliquot match.
Main prose says DCM failed; Figure 5c shows a high DCM yield spoke. Handling: No numerical DCM yield extracted; retain graphical/prose discrepancy.

Scheme 2 lists 11a: 60%*/78%# and 11b: 71%*/85%#, with text methods A/B; no A/B definitions or asterisk legend found in supplied main/SI. Handling: Retain paired yield variants with unresolved method association. Do not infer microwave conditions from instrument listing.

Coumachlor SI procedure names benzylideneacetone, while Scheme 2 R=Cl and product drawing require chlorinated aryl context. Handling: Literal precursor and chlorinated product both retained; no silent reagent substitution.

Main general claim of simple filtration/no chromatography conflicts with SI drug procedures using silica chromatography. Handling: Filtration-only statement applies to scaffold-family procedures; drug workups are separate.
Scheme S2 six-series branch labels NaN3 10 mmol, 0.46 g; four-series branch labels 10 mmol, 0.64 g. Handling: Retain both printed amounts; do not use 0.46 g as a validated 10 mmol conversion.
Scheme S2 reports 9a atom economy 86.93%; detailed SI 33 calculation reports 95.53%. Handling: Separate reported metric contexts.

4e/6e/8e/9e titles say 4-hydroxyphenyl; drawings show 3-bromophenyl and listed masses belong to brominated series. Handling: Retain literal names, source-labelled product IDs and drawn interpretation; molecular identity unresolved.

SI 52 indanedione phenoxy entry is printed 8h; spectrum captions 94–95 label 9h. Handling: Contextual inventory ID 9h is an explicitly marked inference; raw printed 8h retained.

Scope drawings can place phenoxy at a different ring position from the 3-phenoxy names/drawings in characterization (especially 8h Figure S8). Handling: Do not infer exact regioisomer from family letter alone; retain source-specific drawing pointers.

Main 6a CH doublets 6.47–6.48/6.49–6.50 ppm conflict with SI 39 ranges 8.48–8.45/7.60–7.57 ppm; 4a main 6.16 vs SI 34 typed 6.14 while spectrum 55 labels 6.160. Handling: NMR interpretation remains author attribution, not resolved tautomer proof.

operations.description: Measure PL from 80 to 430 K. Fit spectra with Lorentzian functions and extract PL peak energy, FWHM and intensity. The observed trend changes are assigned to γ-tetragonal-1 → β-tetragonal-2 at 140 K and β → α-cubic at 250 K. value.value: Measure PL from 80 to 430 K. Fit spectra with Lorentzian functions and extract PL peak energy, FWHM and intensity. The observed trend changes are assigned to γ-tetragonal-1 → β-tetragonal-2 at 140 K and β → α-cubic at 250 K. These are source interpretations supported by optical/Raman trends, not variable-temperature coordinate refinements on the QDs.

quality.review_scope: Independent main6+matchedSI5 scientific audit of accepted R2 passed. Cited full references remain unreviewed. Presentation refinements pending; no measured-coordinate admission.
missing_fields: Complete supplied six-page main and matched five-page SI read, including all main Figures 1–6, SI Figures S1–S2, seven SI equations, twenty main numbered references/notes and five SI references. Cited full texts remain unreviewed; independent source audit passed; presentation pending.
Core reaction temperature, atmosphere, vessel dimensions, addition rate and stirring speed are unreported. Stirring windows are retained rather than invented exact times.
Size-selective workup lacks solvent amounts, cycle counts, centrifugation speed and duration. Its printed solvent/antisolvent ordering discrepancy is retained.

Film nanocrystal concentration, individual drop volume, drying duration, substrate pretreatment, humidity and gas flow are unreported. Qualitative ambient/room temperature is not converted to a numeric temperature.

Film assembly uses previously synthesized nanocrystals. Exact batch IDs and preparation-to-figure crosswalks are not supplied; solvent conditions are not asserted to be independent new core syntheses. Au Figures 2A–F explicitly share one size fraction.

Superlattice fcc packing concerns nanocrystal organization, not a measurement of the atomic Au/Ag crystal phase, unit cell or atomic coordinates. Model curves and estimated diffusion lengths are not measured product structures.
Pure ethanol is listed among deposition solvents, but no separately resolved pure-ethanol outcome is supplied. No successful pure-ethanol route is invented.

The SI optical experiment has no reported input-particle size or exact link to a particular main-text film batch. Its dilution volume and post-adjustment mass are unreported; optical changes are not new growth/structure evidence.

Original source figures are proposed only under existing owner-directed display; publisher permission remains unverified. Molecule references and stage drawings are conceptual, with complete presentation pending.
conflicts: Detailed Results and Abstract describe the superlattice (111)s plane parallel to the substrate; the Summary instead says normal to the substrate. Structured packing follows the detailed Results and the contrary summary remains explicit.

The workup first identifies ethanol as the antisolvent but subsequently prints ethanol/chloroform as the solvent/antisolvent pair. The ordering discrepancy is retained; no silent solvent-role reversal is made.
The general study size range is 5–7 nm, while the specific Ag Figure 1 caption reports 7.2 ± 0.6 nm. The figure-specific value is not truncated to the rounded general range.
SI calls its absorption coefficient molar absorptivity but reports cm2/mg. The source term and mass-specific units are retained without conversion.

SI Equation 2 defines d as center-to-center distance, whereas Figure S1 labels a 25–50 Å separation-distance axis for 6.3 nm particles. No measured spacing or unambiguous center distance is read from that model plot.

missing_fields: Complete supplied six-page main and matched five-page SI read, including all main Figures 1–6, SI Figures S1–S2, seven SI equations, twenty main numbered references/notes and five SI references. Cited full texts remain unreviewed; independent source audit passed; presentation pending.
Core reaction temperature, atmosphere, vessel dimensions, addition rate and stirring speed are unreported. Stirring windows are retained rather than invented exact times.
Size-selective workup lacks solvent amounts, cycle counts, centrifugation speed and duration. Its printed solvent/antisolvent ordering discrepancy is retained.

Film nanocrystal concentration, individual drop volume, drying duration, substrate pretreatment, humidity and gas flow are unreported. Qualitative ambient/room temperature is not converted to a numeric temperature.

Film assembly uses previously synthesized nanocrystals. Exact batch IDs and preparation-to-figure crosswalks are not supplied; solvent conditions are not asserted to be independent new core syntheses. Au Figures 2A–F explicitly share one size fraction.

Superlattice fcc packing concerns nanocrystal organization, not a measurement of the atomic Au/Ag crystal phase, unit cell or atomic coordinates. Model curves and estimated diffusion lengths are not measured product structures.
Pure ethanol is listed among deposition solvents, but no separately resolved pure-ethanol outcome is supplied. No successful pure-ethanol route is invented.

The SI optical experiment has no reported input-particle size or exact link to a particular main-text film batch. Its dilution volume and post-adjustment mass are unreported; optical changes are not new growth/structure evidence.

Original source figures are proposed only under existing owner-directed display; publisher permission remains unverified. Molecule references and stage drawings are conceptual, with complete presentation pending.
conflicts: Detailed Results and Abstract describe the superlattice (111)s plane parallel to the substrate; the Summary instead says normal to the substrate. Structured packing follows the detailed Results and the contrary summary remains explicit.

The workup first identifies ethanol as the antisolvent but subsequently prints ethanol/chloroform as the solvent/antisolvent pair. The ordering discrepancy is retained; no silent solvent-role reversal is made.
The general study size range is 5–7 nm, while the specific Ag Figure 1 caption reports 7.2 ± 0.6 nm. The figure-specific value is not truncated to the rounded general range.
SI calls its absorption coefficient molar absorptivity but reports cm2/mg. The source term and mass-specific units are retained without conversion.

SI Equation 2 defines d as center-to-center distance, whereas Figure S1 labels a 25–50 Å separation-distance axis for 6.3 nm particles. No measured spacing or unambiguous center distance is read from that model plot.

quality.review_scope: Independently source-audited selected scope: all seven colloidal temperature variants and zinc treatment from main Experimental and SI TableS1, with linked XRD/TEM/EDX/optical results. Downstream film/device/phase-transfer and incomplete ligand-omission controls are explicitly outside this package; retained in private branch inventory. Full independent audit read all 9 main-paper and 9 SI pages. Third-agent sampling and website delivery are tracked separately from this scientific review.
missing_fields: No measured atomic-coordinate asset or definitively resolved cubic/tetragonal distinction.
Most routes have no directly imaged particle shape; TEM distribution only for 130 and 170 °C.
Later centrifugation speeds/times, drying duration, and low-temperature treatment ramp are not reported.
PL spectra and SAXS series remain source figures; unlabelled values were not digitized.
Downstream ligand exchange, film/device procedures and controls are inventoried privately but not claimed as curated routes here.
conflicts: Preferred cubic assignment is qualified by cubic/tetragonal ambiguity and CuAu-type Raman interpretation. ZnS could not be independently distinguished; neither uniform shell nor atomistic interface is established.
Main Figure1a and prose disagree on which XRD method gives 3.2 versus 3.3 nm for the largest sample; retain exact trace label and method-specific text.

quality.review_scope: Independently source-audited selected scope: all seven colloidal temperature variants and zinc treatment from main Experimental and SI TableS1, with linked XRD/TEM/EDX/optical results. Downstream film/device/phase-transfer and incomplete ligand-omission controls are explicitly outside this package; retained in private branch inventory. Full independent audit read all 9 main-paper and 9 SI pages. Third-agent sampling and website delivery are tracked separately from this scientific review.
missing_fields: No measured atomic-coordinate asset or definitively resolved cubic/tetragonal distinction.
Most routes have no directly imaged particle shape; TEM distribution only for 130 and 170 °C.
Later centrifugation speeds/times, drying duration, and low-temperature treatment ramp are not reported.
PL spectra and SAXS series remain source figures; unlabelled values were not digitized.
Downstream ligand exchange, film/device procedures and controls are inventoried privately but not claimed as curated routes here.
conflicts: Preferred cubic assignment is qualified by cubic/tetragonal ambiguity and CuAu-type Raman interpretation. ZnS could not be independently distinguished; neither uniform shell nor atomistic interface is established.
Main Figure1a and prose disagree on which XRD method gives 3.2 versus 3.3 nm for the largest sample; retain exact trace label and method-specific text.

quality.review_scope: Independently source-audited selected scope: all seven colloidal temperature variants and zinc treatment from main Experimental and SI TableS1, with linked XRD/TEM/EDX/optical results. missing_fields: No measured atomic-coordinate asset or definitively resolved cubic/tetragonal distinction.
Most routes have no directly imaged particle shape; TEM distribution only for 130 and 170 °C.
Later centrifugation speeds/times, drying duration, and low-temperature treatment ramp are not reported.
PL spectra and SAXS series remain source figures; unlabelled values were not digitized.
Downstream ligand exchange, film/device procedures and controls are inventoried privately but not claimed as curated routes here.
conflicts: Preferred cubic assignment is qualified by cubic/tetragonal ambiguity and CuAu-type Raman interpretation. ZnS could not be independently distinguished; neither uniform shell nor atomistic interface is established.

value.value: High M/OH (lower pH) favors octahedral Zn monomers; their recoordination may limit tetrahedral-Zn spinel nucleation and permit AlOOH formation. Low M/OH (higher pH) favors ZnO as a tetrahedral-Zn reservoir, with dissolution feeding spinel and residual ZnO as impurity. This is an author mechanism, not directly measured rates or resolved molecular intermediates.

value.value: P02.1 PETRA III total scattering uses a 2D detector, Fit2D integration and PDFgetX3 reduction. Measurements of deionized water in the same capillary type and at the same temperatures supply background. DiffPy CMI is used; PDFgui with LaB6 NIST 660b determines Qdamp.

conflicts: Figure 5 and surrounding prose print deposition charges in mC/cm²; Figures 7 and 9 use µC/cm². The monolayer reference is printed 222 mC/cm². Values and upper-limit equivalent-monolayer estimates remain as printed, without a silent factor-of-1000 correction.

Figure 2 caption and section introduction give 10 mM silver, whereas the Figure 2b discussion and Scheme 1 give 1.0 mM. The general preparation is 1 mM; Figure 3 separately specifies 1.5 mM. These contexts are not merged.
Figure 2d caption names n++-Si whereas its discussion assigns nondegenerate n-Si. The body-based assignment is exposed with this conflict.

Figure 7 contains four displayed histograms and lists four pulse durations, but its caption says five samples. The top panel mean 2.2 nm and sigma 2.4 nm differ from body values 2.4 nm and 2 nm. Four source panels are retained, not a reconstructed fifth specimen.

Figure 8 ordinate is particle density (µm−2) and its discussion concerns nucleation density, while its caption says mean height and height-distribution error bars. The axis/body interpretation is retained with ambiguous error-bar semantics.
Nucleation rates on printed p.797 use cm−2 ms−1, whereas the Summary uses cm−2 s−1. These are separately scoped statements, not a normalized rate label.
Table 1 prints expected FCC Ag (111) d spacing 2.32 Å versus experimental 2.37 Å. No corrected reference value is substituted.

Equation 2 includes an undefined A and does not show the F that appears in Equation 1. Preserve the original equation rather than silently repair it. The text on p.798 refers to Figure 8 for the size–charge model plotted in Figure 9.

conflicts: Figure 2 caption and opening paragraph give 10/10.0 mM Ag+, but detailed n++ discussion and general plating recipe give 1.0 mM. Figure 3 separately gives 1.5 mM.
Figure 2d caption repeats n++-Si while body and comparison identify n-Si. Preserve body/caption distinction.
Figure 5 caption and body print mC/cm² for 1.6/3.6/8.3/18.7 and 222 per monolayer; Figures 7/9 explicitly print µC/cm². Do not silently normalize source charge units.
Equivalent monolayers are upper-bound charge-derived amounts assuming 100% efficiency, not measured planar-area fraction or exact shell thickness.
Four histograms and four listed pulse durations appear, although Figure 7 caption says five samples. Five random image fields per sample is a different count.
First histogram mean/sigma are 2.2/2.4 nm; body gives smallest height 2.4 and spread 2 nm. Largest histogram sigma 6.1 nm versus rounded body 6 nm.
Figure 8 actual ordinate is particle density, not captioned mean height. The height-distribution ±sigma wording cannot establish the density error-bar statistic.
Body nucleation-rate range uses cm−2 ms−1; summary uses cm−2 s−1 with rounded values. Both are retained as conflicting source statements.
Abstract, body and summary give different rounded initial/saturation ranges. Current-model N∞ is approximately an order of magnitude above microscopy density.
Body says no Ag before 2–3 ms while Figure 5 includes a 2 ms image; low-end object density is close to contamination background. No detection-corrected nucleus count is provided.
NC-AFM height is measured; tip-convolved width is not true diameter. Approximately spherical diameter-as-height rationale differs from the hemispherical height-as-radius model.
TEM 10–25 Å objects have unspecified pulse duration and were mechanically transferred. They are not a verified same-sample match to 2–20 nm AFM height populations.
Table 1 expected spacings and intensities are ICDD reference values, not measured specimen intensities. Printed 111 reference spacing is 2.32 Å and must not be silently repaired.
Aqueous instability paragraph names AgO; later phase test contrasts Ag0 with Ag2O. The metallic SAED assignment is retained without creating an oxide synthesis record.
Printed Equation 2 contains A and lacks the explicit F factor present in Equation 1. A is not defined numerically; exact reproduction of N∞ is not supported by note 43 alone.
Band edges were not measured. Barrier energies, depletion widths and geometric N fits are models; z = 1 and hemispherical morphology are assumptions.
Equation 3 discussion refers to Figure 8 predictions, but the model curves are in Figure 9.
Summary says nucleation ceases near 20 ms; body explicitly limits measurements to ≤30 ms and allows undetectably slow continued nucleation on longer times.
TEM method calls 200 keV an accelerating voltage. Preserve the beam setting with its printed energy unit rather than silently transcribing kV.
Figure 2 labels potential in V but numerical ticks and body potentials are in the hundreds of mV. Preserve original axis and use explicit body mV data for typed features.
Step-height ±0.4 Å lacks statistic; Figure 7 sigma denotes height spread; Figure 8 error-bar definition conflicts with its ordinate; Figure 9 ±sigma is height spread, not SEM.
Figure 5, Figure 7, TEM transfer, current transients and the 15-experiment three-day series are source contexts with unknown exact physical sample joins.
Plotted current density includes multiple Faradaic processes; no current efficiency or exact silver mass is established by total charge alone.

operations.description: Place 1.54 g ammonium citrate (reported as 8 mmol) in a 50 mL beaker. Add 15 mL deionized water, 87 µL (1 mmol) MPA and 0.25 g (0.84 mmol) InCl3·4H2O, then stir until completely dissolved. Adjust pH to 7 with 1 M NaOH. Add AgNO3 solution containing 0.03 g (0.16 mmol), followed by 0.38 g (1.60 mmol) Na2S·9H2O. The source reports a deep-brown solution upon full dissolution. Transfer to a cleaned 100 mL three-neck flask.

quality.review_scope: Main PDF pp.1–7 are the extracted scientific scope. The independent full auditor and third-agent corrective auditor accepted the source claims in r10. SI pp.1–7 were inspected as corroborating context; no additional SI-derived numerical extraction is admitted. Presentation and delivery remain pending.
missing_fields: AgNO3 solution volume/concentration; NaOH volume; argon flow; exact batch identity of Figure 1d core XRD; direct AIS-core particle size/morphology; measured atomic coordinates; SI plots not reviewed.
conflicts: Method §2.4 (main p.2) says 96 °C for 45 min for AIS core; Scheme 1 (main p.3) draws 15 min and purification before shell; neither is silently substituted.
Method §2.4 reports ammonium citrate as both 1.54 g and 8 mmol; these values are retained exactly as printed and have not been reconciled to a formula-derived molar mass.
Introduction (main p.2) calls the ligand thioglycolic acid; Materials and §2.4 (main p.2) specify 3-mercaptopropionic acid (MPA).
Figure 1b caption (main p.3) says 95 °C, while §2.4 (main p.2) says 96 °C; the Figure 1b 1:1 Ag:In series is not asserted to be the method batch.
§3.1 (main p.5) assigns orthorhombic AgInS2 yet says a possible alternate orthorhombic AgInS2 or cubic AgIn5S8 cannot be excluded; retain phase ambiguity.

quality.review_scope: Independent complete five-page main scientific audit passed for all seven figures, three tables, equation and eleven references. SI and cited references remain unreviewed. Presentation refinements pending; no measured-coordinate admission.
missing_fields: Complete supplied five-page main read textually and visually. Cited full texts and distinct SI unreviewed. Independent scientific comparison passed; presentation pending.
Nitric acid is 69% but the percentage basis is unspecified. No density, moles, final mixture volume or additive-volume calculation is introduced.

Vigorous/continuous stirring speeds, addition temperature, heating ramps, gas atmosphere, storage duration and vessel closure are unknown unless explicitly stated. Room temperature remains qualitative.

Microwave vessel capacity and cooling/workup are unspecified. Its temperatures are correlations from vaporization enthalpy tables, not measured probe temperatures. TAP is the source abbreviation; its expansion is not defined.
The 2 h cooling and 24 h standing belong only to S2 convection treatment. They are not inherited by S3 or S4.

All samples are split equally; only one half is dried at 80°C for 3 h for analysis. The entire colloidal preparation is not silently converted to dried powder. Exact independent physical batches are unknown.

Scherrer crystallite sizes, TEM particle distributions, Raman peak heights and normalized half-height widths remain distinct. No absolute crystallinity, refined unit cell, atom coordinates or measured CIF is supplied.
Table 3 peak-height units are not printed. Values are retained as source-relative peak heights with unit unknown, not an invented intensity calibration.
Figure 1/7 labels, Figure 6 specimen and brookite reference conflicts remain unresolved. No curve digitization or image-derived size measurement performed.
Source figures have publisher permission unverified; artwork is conceptual. Bibliography identification does not imply reading cited full texts.
conflicts: Table 1 explicitly assigns S3 to 30 psi, correlated 121.5°C and TAP 10 min, and S4 to 60 psi, correlated 145°C and TAP 5 min. Figure 1 and Figure 7 plot keys instead print microwave 5 min at 30 PSI and 10 min at 60 PSI. Table-labeled canonical conditions are preserved alongside the contradictory plot keys; no guessed reconciliation.

Figure 1 caption assigns a=S1 and b=S2, while its plot key labels a=hydrothermally treated and b=colloidal TiO2. Panel-specific sample identity is therefore unresolved; the caption and key remain separate.

Figure 7 caption assigns a=S1, b=S4, c=S3, d=S2; its plot key instead labels a=microwave 5 min 30 PSI, b=microwave 10 min 60 PSI, c=colloidal TiO2, d=hydrothermally treated. No exact curve-to-recipe mapping is silently inferred.

Main p.4 prose identifies the microwave electron-diffraction specimen as S3, but Figure 6 caption identifies S4. Figure 6 is shared ambiguous microwave context and not evidence of a separately identified S3 or S4 physical batch.

Brookite reference is PDF 29-1360 in p.2 prose but PDF 26-1360 in Figure 5 caption. Both printed designations remain visible; no corrected reference number or measured crystallographic file is supplied.

Main p.4 compares 544 W microwave for 12 min with 1300 W convection for 15 h. Methods specify 630 ± 50 W nominal oven power at 80%, 2 min ramp and the Table 1 TAP times. The comparison is attributed source prose, not a substituted power setting or recomputed energy.
The p.3 XRD peak-intensity/defect-plane explanation is preserved as author interpretation. It is not used to infer an absolute defect density or crystallinity percentage.

missing_fields: Complete supplied eight-page main read, including six figures, Scheme 1, Tables 1–3 and 52 numbered references. No matching local SI located; SI and cited full sources unreviewed.
Aqueous ammonia amount, drop rate, stirring speed and exact ambient temperature are unreported. Ammonia concentration is printed as 25% without a stated mass/volume basis.

Sol–gel section states purchased 70 wt% Zr-P, dilution to 30 wt%, precursor 0.025 M and typical 17.7 g Zr-P plus 41.3 g n-propanol. The charge basis and consistency of these statements are unresolved; no molar charge or corrected concentration is calculated.

Vacuum-drying duration, rotation speed, calcination ramp/cooling and furnace/vessel geometry are unreported. Sol–gel washing is not stated; precipitation washing continues until chloride-free but volume/count are unknown.

Scherrer crystallite sizes are author-derived phase/reflection-specific domains, not SEM particle-size distributions. Lattice-strain units/scaling are not stated in Table 2. Blank cells and the printed dash remain explicit missingness rather than inferred zeros.
SEM morphology and N2 isotherms in Figures 5–6 are before calcination. Their shape is not silently transferred to calcined products. Table 3 has only before/400°C values.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending. No measured coordinates or refined unit-cell model supplied.
conflicts: Sol–gel precursor stock/dilution/0.025 M and 17.7 g +41.3 g wording is retained without resolving the charge basis.
Main p.6 prose calls Z-SG-O at700°C 20 nm; Table 2 reports23 nm. Structured values use the explicit table, with the prose discrepancy retained.
Introduction references33 and34 appear interchanged relative to bibliography topics (luminescence versus femoral heads); no external findings become current-product measurements.
SEM operating pressure is printed as >1.34×10−2 Pa; the direction is retained, not silently reversed.
Scheme 1 idealized phase arrows and prose complete transformation (96–100%) are summaries; exact Table 1 fractions, including residual tetragonal phase, take precedence in specimen fields.

quality.review_scope: Independent R3 source audit of all eight supplied main pages, six figures, Scheme 1, Tables 1–3 and the 52-entry bibliography passed. SI and cited references remain unreviewed. Presentation refinements pending; no measured-coordinate admission.
missing_fields: Complete supplied eight-page main read, including six figures, Scheme 1, Tables 1–3 and 52 numbered references. No matching local SI located; SI and cited full sources unreviewed.
Aqueous ammonia amount, drop rate, stirring speed and exact ambient temperature are unreported. Ammonia concentration is printed as 25% without a stated mass/volume basis.

Sol–gel section states purchased 70 wt% Zr-P, dilution to 30 wt%, precursor 0.025 M and typical 17.7 g Zr-P plus 41.3 g n-propanol. The charge basis and consistency of these statements are unresolved; no molar charge or corrected concentration is calculated.

Vacuum-drying duration, rotation speed, calcination ramp/cooling and furnace/vessel geometry are unreported. Sol–gel washing is not stated; precipitation washing continues until chloride-free but volume/count are unknown.

Scherrer crystallite sizes are author-derived phase/reflection-specific domains, not SEM particle-size distributions. Lattice-strain units/scaling are not stated in Table 2. Blank cells and the printed dash remain explicit missingness rather than inferred zeros.
SEM morphology and N2 isotherms in Figures 5–6 are before calcination. Their shape is not silently transferred to calcined products. Table 3 has only before/400°C values.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending. No measured coordinates or refined unit-cell model supplied.
conflicts: Sol–gel precursor stock/dilution/0.025 M and 17.7 g +41.3 g wording is retained without resolving the charge basis.
Main p.6 prose calls Z-SG-O at700°C 20 nm; Table 2 reports23 nm. Structured values use the explicit table, with the prose discrepancy retained.
Introduction references33 and34 appear interchanged relative to bibliography topics (luminescence versus femoral heads); no external findings become current-product measurements.
SEM operating pressure is printed as >1.34×10−2 Pa; the direction is retained, not silently reversed.
Scheme 1 idealized phase arrows and prose complete transformation (96–100%) are summaries; exact Table 1 fractions, including residual tetragonal phase, take precedence in specimen fields.

quality.review_scope: Independent R3 source audit of all eight supplied main pages, six figures, Scheme 1, Tables 1–3 and the 52-entry bibliography passed. SI and cited references remain unreviewed. Presentation refinements pending; no measured-coordinate admission.
missing_fields: Complete supplied eight-page main read, including six figures, Scheme 1, Tables 1–3 and 52 numbered references. No matching local SI located; SI and cited full sources unreviewed.
Aqueous ammonia amount, drop rate, stirring speed and exact ambient temperature are unreported. Ammonia concentration is printed as 25% without a stated mass/volume basis.

Sol–gel section states purchased 70 wt% Zr-P, dilution to 30 wt%, precursor 0.025 M and typical 17.7 g Zr-P plus 41.3 g n-propanol. The charge basis and consistency of these statements are unresolved; no molar charge or corrected concentration is calculated.

Vacuum-drying duration, rotation speed, calcination ramp/cooling and furnace/vessel geometry are unreported. Sol–gel washing is not stated; precipitation washing continues until chloride-free but volume/count are unknown.

Scherrer crystallite sizes are author-derived phase/reflection-specific domains, not SEM particle-size distributions. Lattice-strain units/scaling are not stated in Table 2. Blank cells and the printed dash remain explicit missingness rather than inferred zeros.
SEM morphology and N2 isotherms in Figures 5–6 are before calcination. Their shape is not silently transferred to calcined products. Table 3 has only before/400°C values.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending. No measured coordinates or refined unit-cell model supplied.
conflicts: Sol–gel precursor stock/dilution/0.025 M and 17.7 g +41.3 g wording is retained without resolving the charge basis.
Main p.6 prose calls Z-SG-O at700°C 20 nm; Table 2 reports23 nm. Structured values use the explicit table, with the prose discrepancy retained.
Introduction references33 and34 appear interchanged relative to bibliography topics (luminescence versus femoral heads); no external findings become current-product measurements.
SEM operating pressure is printed as >1.34×10−2 Pa; the direction is retained, not silently reversed.
Scheme 1 idealized phase arrows and prose complete transformation (96–100%) are summaries; exact Table 1 fractions, including residual tetragonal phase, take precedence in specimen fields.

quality.review_scope: Scoped main-text recipe and Figures 1,2,3,5,7 accepted after full independent review of main pp.1–12 and SI pp.1–17, and corrective source/asset checks. SI was read as context; this package does not extract every SI result. Presentation and delivery are pending.
missing_fields: Exact Cd and S stock aliquot volumes for each of nine SILAR shell cycles are not reported in the inspected main text; Ref.22 not independently extracted.
Main text gives quantified 10 wt% polymer composite; 5, 20 and 25 wt% comparisons lack equivalent charge details and are contextual, not extra pairs.
The 3-decyl-1-vinylimidazolium chloride monomer preparation is not described in main Methods.
No measured atomic coordinates or coherent CdSe/CdS interface model; unit cells are separate bulk references.
TEM of recovered polymerized QDs is described but data not shown in main; SI not inspected.
Shell-growth OA chemical identity, Methods/Figure 1A ligand durations and binding solvent remain unresolved source conflicts; do not train on one chosen branch.
conflicts: p.3 CdSe Cores paragraph calls estimated QDs 10 nm; p.4 Results assigns ~4 nm CdSe cores and nine CdS monolayers, while p.5 SAXS yields 10.3 nm diameter for the core-shell QDs. Preserve wording and referent ambiguity.
p.3 heading labels QD-bound imidazolium conjugate with [Cl−]; p.3 prose and Figure 1A identify bromide counterion. Counterion of surface species unresolved.

p.3 SeTOP stock is labelled 0.2 M, but 2.36 g Se in 15 mL TOP gives ~1.99 M using TOP volume as a proxy; final stock volume is unknown. Both source claims and calculation are retained; actual stock and injected Se molarity unresolved.
For the separate free 3-decyl-1-vinylimidazolium monomer, p.3 and p.4 prose name chloride while Figure 1B draws Br− for compound (4). Its counterion is independently unresolved.
p.4 gives native QD PL FWHM 29 nm; p.6 PL comparison gives native FWHM 35 nm. Both statements retained.
p.3 reports 19 mg water and calls final composition 30 ± 2 wt%; 19/(4.5+40.5+19)=29.69% calculated, compatible but do not replace reported range.

Thiol precursor Methods (main p.3) give KOH in EtOH 2 h and HCl 10% v/v stir 1 h; Figure 1A (main p.4) instead gives KOH/EtOH reflux 12 h and HCl 2 h. Both branches retained without choosing or averaging.

Thiol binding Methods (main p.3) use 5 mL ACN and 2 h standing; Figure 1A (main p.4) shows DMF at room temperature for 2 h, with no DMF amount. Both source branches retained; the operation inputs describe Methods only.

Main p.2 Materials abbreviates oleylamine 70% as OA, whereas main p.3 stock methods expand OA as oleic acid 90%. Shell-growth line says 5 mL OA without expansion; its exact shell-feed chemical identity is unresolved.
Main p.3 prints Mg2SO4 for the drying agent. The conventional MgSO4 interpretation is plausible but unverified; no source formula is silently corrected.
Main p.1 abstract reports composite PL maximum 638 nm; main p.6 comparison reports 637 nm for the 10 wt% composite. Both source values retained; the numeric measurement uses p.6 context.

Collection technique, wash amounts/repetitions, dilute-acetic-acid concentration, vacuum level, drying apparatus, yield and storage are unreported. Wash order is absolute ethanol, distilled water, dilute acetic acid, then acetone.

Figure 2 explicitly depicts the same sample as Figure 1. No physical batch identifier, TEM specimen preparation/grid, XRD holder, particle-count statistic, size uncertainty or distribution width is given. Average TEM particle size is 30 nm; no XRD crystallite size is reported.

Benzene and tetrahydrofuran controls give neither a homogeneous selenium-containing solution nor PbSe under irradiation. Their charges, irradiation dose/time and subsequent processing are not individually stated and are not copied from the successful ethylenediamine route.

Formation chemistry is explicitly unknown and the solvent/solvated-electron explanation is proposed. No intermediate, kinetic rate, product atomic coordinates or current optical/electronic property measurement is supplied.

quality.review_scope: Primary 5 mL silica-route preparation, stated product, qualified figure/sample links; core-only extraction accepted by a different full source auditor. Other variants are pending.
missing_fields: This is a core-only extraction of the standard 5 mL ethanol, single-loading silica route with the thin meso-P25 substrate preparation. Other variants remain pending with exact source locators.

Substrate dimensions, initial P25 stirring time, substrate spin-coating duration, dispensed precursor volume, 65 °C dwell and final CdO–silica calcination dwell are not reported in the corresponding detailed Methods paragraphs.
The 450 °C/1 h statement in the multiple-loading discussion is not silently transferred to the single-loading Methods route.
Nitric acid is named in the silica precursor description but its silica-stage charge is omitted from the detailed formulation. The separate 0.5 g, 65% acid charge belongs to the meso-P25 preparation.

No exact physical batch links join thin-substrate preparation to every microscopy specimen; Figure 4 III identifies the 5 mL formulation, while TEM size and fringes describe the broader silica-system sample context.

H2Se source/generation, gas quantity, chamber volume, numerical initial vacuum and a quantitative carrier-gas mixture are not reported. Source apparatus is a vacuum chamber designed for this reaction; this literature record is not a complete operating procedure.
The isolated CdSe yield, particle concentration and measured atomic coordinates are not reported. Solar-cell efficiency is outside the scoped as-prepared film product.
conflicts: Silica-stage acid: Results p.4983 lists nitric acid in the infiltrated silica precursor; detailed silica formulation p.4988 lists no acid charge. Both statements remain visible, without borrowing the meso-P25 acid amount.

Comparator ethanol amount: Figure 4 caption p.4985 labels pattern II as 2.5 mL, whereas the synthesis formulation p.4988 lists alternative 3 mL. The primary 5 mL pattern III is unaffected; no comparator values are normalized.

Conversion atmosphere: detailed Methods p.4989 states chamber evacuation then about 100 Torr H2Se; Conclusions p.4988 summarizes N2/H2Se. No N2 pressure or mixture is inferred for the detailed conversion.

quality.review_scope: Independent scientific review of both supplied main pages, four figures, Table I and the six-reference bibliography passed without findings. One method supports seven partial size-labelled outcomes; exact per-size schedules and batches remain unresolved. SI and cited references remain unreviewed. Presentation refinements pending; no measured-coordinate admission.
missing_fields: Complete supplied two-page main only; any SI and all cited full references unreviewed.

Reagent masses, molar ratios, solution volumes/concentrations and PEG-solution solvent are not reported. PEG molecular weight is given as 20 000 without a distribution or specified molecular-weight average.
Dehydration/decomposition durations and atmospheres, calcination ramp/cooling and product workup are not reported.
The common 250–800 °C / 2–6 h range is not mapped to individual crystal-size outcomes; no seven exact thermal recipes or distinct physical batches are invented.
Average crystal size is evaluated by XRD and TEM, but no TEM image, morphology distribution, lattice parameter, refinement, unit-cell coordinates or exact specimen identifiers are supplied.
Magnetization and coercivity plots are retained without digitization. Figure 2 trace-to-sample assignments and Figure 4 symbol-to-size mapping are not resolved in the main.
Source-specific molecular, morphology and unit-cell presentation remain pending where a reliable reference or unique identity is not available.
conflicts: Figure 3 caption gives five lettered size labels, while the plotted graph shows unlabeled points; no transfer of these letters onto Figure 2 is assumed.
Figure 4 caption prints an anomalous Oe-to-A/m relation; no conversion of its Oe-axis values is performed.

The methods describe magnetic measurements from ambient temperature to 700 °C, while Figure 4 displays a 150–350 K range. These different source contexts are retained without an inferred low-temperature method.

quality.review_scope: Two linked source-reported preparations: required solvothermal PbS powder and primary Sample C PbS/carbon-black composite counter electrode, PbS:CB 10:1 by weight. Included product evidence comprises PbS powder phase/size, incoming CB particle-size context, Sample C film morphology/thickness, and the named Sample C symmetric-cell EIS context with 2 M Na2S plus 2 M S. Other ratios, devices, electrolyte variants and stability applications remain explicitly pending. Exact physical batches across preparations and characterization are not established.

Other ratios, devices, electrolyte variants and stability applications remain explicitly pending. Exact physical batches across preparations and characterization are not established.

Drying atmosphere/ramp and CE storage unreported.

missing_fields: Matching supporting information not located or verified.
No atomic coordinates, exact physical batch IDs or complete specimen-to-batch joins supplied.
No raw particle list, digitized curve, complete statistical uncertainty, refined structure, or exact specimen linkage supplied.
Figure 1 panel a/b labels are time panels, independent of preparation sample a/b labels.
Cited model inputs reproduce the current paper only; the cited references have not all been independently read.
conflicts: The recipe explicitly pretreats with 10 mL of 0.5 M NaCl and then adds 100 mL aqueous sulfide, while figures/model retain a 0.5 M label. The final reaction-mixture concentration is not clearly reconciled. Preserve stock/preload concentration and source cohort label; do not silently calculate or impose a final 0.5 M concentration.
Figure 5a gives log-normal SD 0.4 without unit or parameter definition. Store value with unit null and raw wording; avoid converting it into diameter error bars.
The hypothetical swelling calculation prints −26 meV although surrounding Δφ values use mV. Keep original unit and mark the dimension conflict.
A finite −390 mV is reported for zero added NaCl, but the outside concentration C used for background ions is not explicitly given. Do not claim a numerically reproduced model without this input.
Note 33 refers to anions in a positively charged polymer; main model describes a cation-exchange resin. Keep this as source-context ambiguity, not corrected physical proof.

The abstract describes a formation rate proportional to sqrt(time), but Figure 8 and body fit absorbance itself against sqrt(time). Represent the observed ordinate as absorbance; do not turn its slope into dA/dt.
Figure 2 uses filled circles for salt and open circles for no salt; Figures 8–9 use the reverse. Bind marker identity separately for each figure.
Figure 1 panels a/b mean 30 min/48 h, whereas the preparation sample labels a/b mean no salt/salt. Keep both independent dimensions of identity.
XRD means, TEM fitted regional means, constituent-crystal ranges, and aggregate descriptions concern different methods/scopes. No single universal size target and no invented exact specimen joins.
100–110 um is host diameter; micrometer depths/L describe CdS location in that host; nanometer sizes describe CdS constituent crystals. Use separate typed properties, not one size field.
The optical plateau within 2 h for b is not the end of the preparative 2 h stir plus 2 day standing sequence. Store protocol durations separately from the observed optical-progress interpretation.

The HS− coefficients use an optical L proxy and diffusion scaling; Na+ diffusion is a cited resin-context value associated with Chelex 100, and Donnan potential values are model calculations. Keep separate species, methods, and evidence classes.

Absorbance trends and similar early spectral shapes support qualitative formation/size interpretations, not absolute CdS yields or exact spectral peak targets. No curve digitization, mass-yield inference, band-gap conversion, or universal 450 nm calibration.

quality.review_scope: Independent scoped scientific quick audit accepted the complete locally matched main PDF pp.1–2 and SI pp.1–11 for the packaged CdSe precursor and TNM gel route, full Ag2Se exchange and drying, the separate partial-Ag wet-gel illustration, PbSe/CuSe analog branches, main Figures 1–3/Table 1 and SI Figures S1–S7. The main/SI concentration and gel-timing disagreements, unreported partial/analog doses, and Figure S4 contents conflict remain explicit. Earlier cited Peng, Aldana and Arachchige papers were not imported.
missing_fields: Exact Ag+ dose, exchange time and workup for Figure 1B partial exchange are not reported.
Pb(NO3)2 and Cu(NO3)2 concentrations and solution volumes are not restated for the analog routes.
The paper does not report quantitative PbSe/CuSe EDS ratios or pore metrics.
The exact TNM oxidative bridge topology, thiolate surface coverage and atomistic cation locations are not measured.
The 36° Ag2Se diffraction feature may include disorder or a secondary amorphous component; no unique assignment is made.
The full Ag2Se drying is said to follow CdSe SI conditions; distinct Ag2Se dryer settings are not restated.
conflicts: Main p.1 gives nominal Cd2+ concentration 0.025 M and AgNO3 0.15 M, a sixfold numerical ratio, while SI p.3 calls 0.15 M AgNO3 '5 times the nominal Cd2+ concentration'. Preserve both published statements; do not repair the ratio silently.
Main p.1 waits 12 h after adding Ag+ before methanol wash; SI p.3 says Ag2Se wet gel develops after 'a few hours'. These are distinct described endpoints and are both retained.
The text layer misrecognizes α-Ag2Se as R-Ag2Se. Original PDF page rendering visually confirms Greek α in main p.1–2.
Main Figure 2 insets are reference crystal diagrams; they are not measured atomic structures of the pictured aerogels.
SI contents p.1 calls Figure S4 porosimetry of CdSe and Ag2Se, but actual Figure S4 caption/plot on p.8 shows Ag2Se only; no CdSe S4 curve is assigned.

value.value: Authors attribute performance gains to larger CdS/PbS interfacial area, direct transport through ordered CdS rods and shorter carrier diffusion paths. Proposed follow-up: tune rod crystallinity, spacing/length and contacts.

Open first funnel to inject lithium silylamide solution
After10s delay inject DIBAL solution from second funnel
At50°C add chloroform and oleic acid, then precipitate with ethanol

Perform source-optional additional repeat of second wash

quality.review_scope: All five supplied main pages text-read and visually inspected, with independent source, canonical, molecular, apparatus and reader audits. Five hydrothermal annealing comparisons, independent solid-state bulk preparation, stock preparation, structural/optical analyses and author mechanisms retain their own evidence scopes. Printed mass/mole and nominal feed/formula conflicts, individual comparison charges and unassigned analysis specimens remain explicit. missing_fields: No verified SI, raw spectral arrays, atomic coordinates, refined dopant occupancies or absolute quantum yield is supplied.
Physical batch identifiers and most characterization specimen preparation/settings are absent; general figure context is not a per-run sample join.

Diluted nitric acid concentration/volume, stock pH, hydrothermal pressure/ramp/cooling, wash volume, air-drying duration/temperature, annealing atmosphere, isolated yield and sample mass are unreported.
conflicts: Printed ammonium molybdate identity (NH4)2MoO4, 1.961 g and 9.37 mmol are inconsistent. The reported Mo and rare-earth amounts also do not directly match nominal La2(MoO4)3 stoichiometry; no correction or actual product occupancy is inferred.

quality.review_scope: All five supplied main pages text-read and visually inspected, with independent source, canonical, molecular, apparatus and reader audits. Five hydrothermal annealing comparisons, independent solid-state bulk preparation, stock preparation, structural/optical analyses and author mechanisms retain their own evidence scopes. Printed mass/mole and nominal feed/formula conflicts, individual comparison charges and unassigned analysis specimens remain explicit. Matching SI not located or verified; cited external works not independently inspected.
missing_fields: No verified SI, raw spectral arrays, atomic coordinates, refined dopant occupancies or absolute quantum yield is supplied.
Physical batch identifiers and most characterization specimen preparation/settings are absent; general figure context is not a per-run sample join.

Diluted nitric acid concentration/volume, stock pH, hydrothermal pressure/ramp/cooling, wash volume, air-drying duration/temperature, annealing atmosphere, isolated yield and sample mass are unreported.
conflicts: Printed ammonium molybdate identity (NH4)2MoO4, 1.961 g and 9.37 mmol are inconsistent. The reported Mo and rare-earth amounts also do not directly match nominal La2(MoO4)3 stoichiometry; no correction or actual product occupancy is inferred.

missing_fields: Per-composition precursor masses/moles for each Cu/Zn ratio are not in supplied main/SI.
Copper acetate mass/mole conflict unresolved; no silent correction.

Ramp rates, post-injection temperature transitions, pressure, flask capacity, stirring rate, injection rate/duration, product yield, methanol volumes/counts, final solvent and storage before characterization are not specified.
SI figure annotations SH=2 mmol are undefined; do not equate to DDT or another input.
No unit-cell, CIF, coordinate file, lattice parameters, space group or refined phase fractions; only author-assigned common “zinc blend” peaks.
Main p.2 HRTEM citation points to SI S2 while actual HRTEM is S4; sample temperature/composition for S4 not identified.

Figure 3A is labeled 150 °C; the remaining unresolved point is how the 210 °C preheat transitions to each selected post-injection hold and the final 230 °C heating stage. Ramp rates and transition details are unspecified.
Figure 1D/Figure 2 include a 150 °C specimen beyond three Figure 1 TEM specimens; main prose calls diffraction samples “three”.
Quantitative size distributions, ratio-specific sizes, QY table, PL lifetime fits and exact Figure S6 y-values are absent.
SI S5/Table S1 captions say temperatures while visible sample labels are ratios; exact per-sample batch/recipe amounts are absent.
Source extraction independently reviewed through R1 plus R2 delta. This canonical/Reader projection requires a separate integration-mapping review.
Source figure permission remains unverified; no measured atomic coordinates or training admission are supplied.
conflicts: Preserve supplier wording and Methods wording separately. Printed mass and mole are internally inconsistent; neither is corrected.

Keep the Methods sequence exactly (initial 210 °C until clear, sulfur injection, selected 150/180/210/240 °C hold, then 230 °C for 5 min). Figure 3A first trace is 150 °C and agrees with Figures 1D, 2, and 4. The Methods do not explain the temperature transitions (including how the 150 °C hold follows the 210 °C preheat) or ramp rates; do not invent a monotonic or corrected sequence.
Actual SI labels HRTEM S4; S2 is In2S3 absorption/XRD. Bind to actual caption and preserve the mismatch.
TEM A–C are three explicit specimens; Figure1D and Figure2 show four temperatures including 150 °C. The three-sample prose does not explain the extra 150 °C XRD/EDS trace.
S5/Table S1 captions say “obtained under different reaction temperatures” but visible legend/columns are Cu/Zn ratios. Main text links these to composition series EDX; preserve caption mismatch.

The printed prose reports 620–750 nm for 2.0–7.0 nm particles. Figure 3B visually presents the same trend but its plotted endpoints do not map exactly to the prose range. Preserve this qualitative graph/prose discrepancy only; no digitized point values or new numeric rows are supported.

Source extraction independently reviewed through R1 plus R2 delta. This canonical/Reader projection requires a separate integration-mapping review.
Source figure permission remains unverified; no measured atomic coordinates or training admission are supplied.
conflicts: Preserve supplier wording and Methods wording separately. Printed mass and mole are internally inconsistent; neither is corrected.

Keep the Methods sequence exactly (initial 210 °C until clear, sulfur injection, selected 150/180/210/240 °C hold, then 230 °C for 5 min). Figure 3A first trace is 150 °C and agrees with Figures 1D, 2, and 4. The Methods do not explain the temperature transitions (including how the 150 °C hold follows the 210 °C preheat) or ramp rates; do not invent a monotonic or corrected sequence.
Actual SI labels HRTEM S4; S2 is In2S3 absorption/XRD. Bind to actual caption and preserve the mismatch.

quality.review_scope: Independently audited main-text sequential CdTe–CdSe nanocrystal growth, purification/specimen branches, pyridine exchange, single-SNCH and 90 wt% hybrid device routes, optical blend controls and Figures 1–9 across main pages 1–6. Cited upstream studies and unavailable SI were not audited. Source conflicts, missing parameters and specimen distinctions remain explicit; this is scoped content acceptance.
missing_fields: Growth atmosphere, degassing pressure, Cd acetate hydration, exact OPA and ODE identities are unresolved.
Per-addition Se stock volume/amount and interval reference points are not explicit.
Purification volumes, centrifugation conditions and number of repetitions are not quantified.
No sample-specific atomic-coordinate file or explicitly named crystal polytype is supplied.
No single full-run timing schedule reconciles all source statements.
conflicts: Growth temperature: Methods p.2 section 2.2 reports 240 °C; Results p.2 section 3.1 reports 250 °C. Unresolved.
Branch sizes: abstract p.1 and Results p.2 report thickness 3–5 nm and length 10–30 nm; Conclusions p.6 reports 3–4 nm and 5–30 nm. Unresolved.

Spectral time origins: Figure 6 plot labels II 45 min and III 75 min, while its caption specifies 15 min reaction after each respective injection; p.3 body describes first addition for 30 min. These are retained as source timing descriptions, not independently resolved schedules.
Absorption coverage: abstract p.1 states 380–780 nm; photovoltaic discussion p.4 states 380–750 nm.
